stories.headline: China warns of new global chip shortage as Nexperia locks Chinese staff out of IT systems

key_facts.fact: China's commerce ministry on March 7 raised the possibility of another global semiconductor supply chain crisis due to 'new conflicts' between Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its Chinese subsidiary
key_facts.excerpt: China's commerce ministry on Saturday raised the possibility of another global semiconductor supply chain crisis due to 'new conflicts' between Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its Chinese subsidiary

key_facts.fact: Nexperia's Chinese packaging arm accused the Netherlands-based headquarters of disabling office accounts for all employees in China, which China's ministry said 'provoked new conflicts and created further obstacles to the ongoing negotiation process'
key_facts.excerpt: By disabling the office accounts of its employees in China, Nexperia has provoked new conflicts and created further obstacles to the ongoing negotiation process

key_facts.fact: Production across the global auto industry was disrupted in October 2025 when Beijing imposed export controls on Chinese-made Nexperia chips after the Dutch government seized the company from its Chinese parent Wingtech
key_facts.excerpt: Production across the global auto industry was disrupted in October when Beijing imposed export controls on Chinese-made Nexperia chips after The Hague seized the company from its Chinese parent Wingtech

key_facts.fact: China's ministry warned that the Dutch side 'must bear full responsibility should these measures trigger another crisis in the global semiconductor industry and its supply chains'
key_facts.excerpt: The Dutch side must bear full responsibility should these measures trigger another crisis in the global semiconductor industry and its supply chains

key_facts.fact: Wingtech's parent is seeking $8 billion in compensation over the Dutch government's seizure of Nexperia, which it called an 'unprecedented action'
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia owner to seek $8 billion compensation in semiconductor showdown as Dutch block China control

stories.headline: Ukraine fields world's first armed ground robot battalion as UGV demand projected to hit 40,000 in 2026

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's K2 Brigade has stood up the world's first dedicated UGV battalion, commanded by Major Oleksandr Afanasiev, deploying armed ground robots with Kalashnikov machine guns and grenade launchers
key_facts.excerpt: Robot wars are already happening, says Oleksandr Afanasiev from the Ukrainian army's K2 brigade. He commands its UGV battalion — the world's first, he says

key_facts.fact: The battalion deploys battery-powered kamikaze UGVs that roll silently toward enemy positions and detonate — unlike aerial drones, they produce no audible warning
key_facts.excerpt: His battalion has also been using explosive-laden, battery-powered kamikaze UGVs to blow up enemy positions and hideouts. Unlike aerial drones that buzz overhead, they make no sound

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian manufacturer Devdroid produced hundreds of 'strike droids' in 2025 and is developing AI-powered systems with Browning machine guns for autonomous target tracking at distances up to 300 meters
key_facts.excerpt: The Droid TW family of UGVs is currently being utilized to engage targets from distances up to 300 meters, integrating AI tracking with mounted Browning machine guns

key_facts.fact: Manufacturer Tencore produced over 2,000 UGVs in 2025 and expects demand to jump to approximately 40,000 units in 2026, with 10-15% armed with weapons
key_facts.excerpt: Tencore produced more than 2,000 UGVs for the Ukrainian army in 2025, with its director expecting demand to jump to around 40,000 units in 2026, at least 10-15% of them armed

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian and Russian killer robots have clashed without humans present at the battle site, and UGVs have successfully repelled Russian attacks and taken enemy soldiers prisoner
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian and Russian killer robots are even said to have clashed without humans being present at the site of the battle

key_facts.fact: The kill zone on Ukraine's eastern front has pushed out to roughly 15 km from the line of contact, making infantry advances a 'casualty guarantee'
key_facts.excerpt: The kill zone on Ukraine's eastern front has pushed out to roughly 15 kilometers from the line of contact. At that distance, sending infantry forward isn't a tactical decision anymore

stories.headline: NASA selects ULA's Centaur V to replace cancelled Boeing upper stage for Artemis IV and V moon missions

key_facts.fact: NASA awarded a sole-source contract to United Launch Alliance for its Centaur V upper stage to power Artemis IV and V missions, replacing the cancelled Boeing Exploration Upper Stage
key_facts.excerpt: NASA has selected the Centaur upper stage currently used on United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket for future Space Launch System missions

key_facts.fact: The JOFOC was signed March 6 by NASA Senior Procurement Executive Marvin Horne at Marshall Space Flight Center, confirming ULA's Centaur V as the sole viable replacement
key_facts.excerpt: The JOFOC signed March 6 by NASA Senior Procurement Executive Marvin Horne confirms that ULA's Vulcan Centaur V upper stage will replace the long-planned Exploration Upper Stage

key_facts.fact: The original EUS development was cancelled on February 27, 2026, when NASA discontinued the Block 1B SLS version — its costs had ballooned to nearly $2.8 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The original EUS development was cancelled February 27, 2026, when NASA discontinued the Block 1B SLS version

key_facts.fact: The contract covers two flight units for Artemis IV and V plus one flight spare, leveraging the already-operational Centaur stage flying on ULA's Vulcan rocket
key_facts.excerpt: Missions covered: Artemis 4 and 5, plus one flight spare

key_facts.fact: The current Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage used on Artemis 1-3 cannot be replenished because its production line, based on Delta 4 heritage, is permanently closed
key_facts.excerpt: The current Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage, used on Artemis 1-3, cannot be replenished because its production line — based on Delta 4 heritage — is permanently closed

stories.headline: Gulf AI data center ambitions under threat as Iran drone strikes reveal new vulnerability in digital infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Iranian drone strikes damaged three Amazon Web Services data centers in the UAE and Bahrain, marking the first known military attack on a hyperscale cloud provider's infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: A strike on the UAE facility marks the first time a major U.S. tech company's data center has been disrupted by military action

key_facts.fact: The strikes knocked two of the ME-CENTRAL-1 region's three availability zones offline, triggering outages across EC2, S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, RDS and other core AWS services in the Gulf
key_facts.excerpt: The strikes knocked two of the ME-CENTRAL-1 region's three availability zones offline, leaving the region significantly impaired

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC claimed responsibility, with Iranian state media saying the Amazon data center was targeted for the company's support of 'U.S. military and intelligence activities'
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's Bahrain data center was targeted by Iran for the company's support of 'U.S. military and intelligence activities,' the Fars News Agency said

key_facts.fact: The Guardian reported on March 7 that experts now warn Gulf data center buildouts may require missile defense systems, questioning the region's viability as an AI superpower
key_facts.excerpt: It means missile defence on data centres: drone strikes raises doubts over Gulf as AI superpower

key_facts.fact: Over 200 data centers operate across the Middle East; Gulf nations had planned $300+ billion in AI infrastructure investment now imperiled by the conflict
key_facts.excerpt: There are over 200 data centers across the Middle East, and cheap energy and land have drawn U.S. hyperscalers to pour resources into building out capacity in the region

key_facts.fact: Carnegie fellow Sam Winter-Levy said: 'Cloud infrastructure was always theoretically vulnerable to kinetic warfare, but nobody had priced that risk in so far. Now that has to change'
key_facts.excerpt: Cloud infrastructure was always theoretically vulnerable to kinetic warfare, but nobody had priced that risk in so far. Now that has to change

stories.headline: AI data center boom drives $22B power line buildout across US, sparking fierce local backlash

key_facts.fact: A $22 billion transmission package in the Midwest grid territory is embroiled in opposition from utility regulators in North Dakota, Montana, Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana
key_facts.excerpt: A $22 billion transmission package is embroiled in a monthlong fight, as utility regulators in North Dakota, Montana, Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana urge federal regulators to block it

key_facts.fact: Pennsylvania's state consumer advocate is protesting a $1.7 billion proposed line spanning more than 200 miles from West Virginia to connect coal-fired power plants to data center alley in northern Virginia
key_facts.excerpt: Pennsylvania's state consumer advocate is protesting a $1.7 billion proposed transmission line spanning more than 200 miles from West Virginia across half of Pennsylvania

key_facts.fact: Utility transmission spending is projected to double to nearly $50 billion per year from 2019 to 2028, driven primarily by data center power needs
key_facts.excerpt: Utility transmission spending projected to double to nearly $50 billion a year from 2019 to 2028

key_facts.fact: PPL Electric projects peak electricity demand in eastern Pennsylvania will more than triple by 2030 due to data center development, driven by Amazon's expansion
key_facts.excerpt: PPL projects peak electricity demand in eastern Pennsylvania will more than triple by 2030 due to data center development

key_facts.fact: Texas is planning three 765-kilovolt lines — the highest voltage in the U.S. — as east-west 'superhighway' corridors to power data centers in the Hill Country
key_facts.excerpt: Three 765-kilovolt lines, the highest voltage in the U.S., proposed as east-west superhighway corridors across the state

stories.headline: SpaceX launches 25 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg, constellation passes 9,900 operational satellites

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 25 Starlink satellites from SLC-4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base on March 8, 2026 at 7:00 AM EDT (4:00 AM PDT)
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched 25 Starlink satellites from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base on March 8, 2026

key_facts.fact: Booster B1097 completed its seventh flight and landed on the droneship 'Of Course I Still Love You' in the Pacific Ocean
key_facts.excerpt: The Falcon's first stage, Booster 1097, completed its seventh spaceflight with a landing on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship

key_facts.fact: The Starlink constellation now has 11,463 total launched, 9,924 currently in orbit, and 9,913 operational satellites
key_facts.excerpt: Total launched: 11,463. Currently in orbit: 9,924. Operational: 9,913

key_facts.fact: West Coast launches from Vandenberg target polar or high-inclination orbits to fill coverage gaps at higher latitudes for the broadband constellation
key_facts.excerpt: West Coast launches like this typically target polar or high-inclination orbits to fill coverage gaps at higher latitudes

stories.headline: Plug Power plans 250 MW hydrogen offering in PJM grid auction to power AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Plug Power is planning to offer up to 250 megawatts of hydrogen electricity in a potential special auction by PJM, the biggest US power grid, to feed AI data center demand
key_facts.excerpt: Plug Power Inc. is planning to offer hydrogen electricity in a potential special auction by the biggest US power grid in the scramble to feed the artificial intelligence boom

key_facts.fact: Plug Power chairman Andy Marsh said the company would need contracts lasting at least seven years and is already in talks with hyperscalers, data center companies and utilities
key_facts.excerpt: Plug would need contracts lasting at least seven years, and is already talking to hyperscalers, data center companies and utilities

key_facts.fact: President Trump is keen for the PJM special auction to happen later this year, as data center power demand strains the US grid
key_facts.excerpt: Considering providing as much as 250 megawatts in an auction that President Donald Trump is keen to happen later this year

key_facts.fact: Plug Power separately signed a $132.5 million deal with Stream Data Centers for its Project Gateway site in New York, part of over $275 million in planned asset monetization
key_facts.excerpt: Plug expects to receive gross proceeds of at least $132.5 million, with total proceeds of up to $142 million depending on the timing of closing
